correctness.rationale: For fixed p and deterministic distinct Gaussian scores, edge independence gives P(L_n>s|Z)=(1-p)^{N_n(s;Z)} for 0<=s<R. Upper and reflected lower Gaussian rare extremes converge jointly to independent PPPs intensity e^-x dx, so near-maximal spanning pairs and independent Bernoulli marks converge to finite candidate count N_t with EN_t=(t+1)e^t. Thus sqrt(2log n)L_n converges to D_p. The first edge from the maximum to ordered minima is geometric(p), and uniform Gaussian top-order-statistic second moment bounds imply uniform integrability, permitting convergence of means. Gaussian radial-direction separation in H_n gives factor sqrt(2) in intrinsic mean-width deficit. Monotone coupling and first-gap analysis show c(p) strictly decreasing, c(p)~log(1/p) near zero, c(p)~(1-p)/2 near one. Exact n=4 graph subset tail check supports the Bernoulli identity; no finite simulation proves Poisson or mean convergence.
